summary: PAPER-CHEN-24 is a thorough extraction of arXiv v2 of Chen's Annals paper: 123 items, 6 routes and 38 source issues. Its review was deep, and all 38 issues stand on recheck. Recomputation for every prime p ≤ 89 confirms the §5.6 claims: the E1 count, the genus formula, the cusp count, and the S/A parity rule of Theorem 5.6.6 mod 16. There are 10 findings: 6 medium and 4 low. Medium: (1) a missed error in Theorem 5.6.4 and Theorem 1.2.9. The Faltings consequence 'only finitely many elliptic curves over K admit an SL₂(F_p)-structure (cover) with ramification index 2p' is false over K, because such structures are invariant under quadratic twist: (AB − BA)/2 ∈ SL₂(F_p) conjugates (A, B) to (A⁻¹, B⁻¹) when tr[A,B] = −2. Only finitely many j-invariants is what is proved; items 16 and 97 state it over K. (2) The version of record, revised in July 2022, was never read. sourceVersions is missing, and data/collation.json misclassifies the paper as read from the published text, so it is absent from the collation worklist. (3) Out(F₂) ≅ GL₂(ℤ), the Nielsen generators of Aut(F₂) and Mod_{1,1} ≅ Out⁺(Π) duplicate Landesman–Litt's new mapping-class-group roadmap, accepted 34 minutes after this review. The Nielsen generators have no item, and item 107 overclaims Out(Π) as library. (4) The Hurwitz stack of G-covers of (g,n)-curves, étale over M_{g,n} with Z(G) isotropy, is planned by IG.5, by Landesman–Litt 125 and, in the (1,1) case and in general-(g,n) items 21/23/33, by route 6. (5) The accepted source routes never reached the live blueprint issues (#1025, #1013, #1020). CA.4 was closed as source_decomposed without the coefficient-one surface 𝕏 and the twist ξ that routes 2 and 6 import from it, and route 6 still names the superseded ArithmeticDynamicsPartIIMarkoff. (6) The review widened item 112 to Riemann existence for stacks but kept it planned at IG.3/BelyiMaps layer 8, which plan only curves. Low: missing prerequisites (Brumfiel–Hilden, Deligne 1989, Magnus–Karrass–Solitar, Osborne–Zieschang, Knudsen) and two small inputs; four wrong library names or paths (CategoryTheory.FiberFunctor among them); two missed misprints; and the route 6 brief is out of sync with the item 52 correction, while item 2's planned citations are imprecise. Disclosure: this session red-teamed Gamburd–Magee–Ronan 19 and Ellenberg–Venkatesh–Westerland 16. Finding 5 shares a mechanism with GMR19 finding 7; no other finding relies on them.

Computations (a script over F_p for every prime 5 ≤ p ≤ 89). |𝕏*(p)| = p(p+3) or p(p−3). Aut(Π) and Aut⁺(Π) are transitive on 𝕏*(p) for every such p. |f⁻¹(0)| = (deg f + 2)/3 with exactly one γ₀-fixed point (E1). |f⁻¹(1728)| and its 0 or 2 fixed points match Proposition 5.6.1(b) and the p ≡ 1, 7 mod 8 rule. The rot₁-orbit count equals Proposition 5.3.5's formula. The Riemann–Hurwitz genus equals Theorem 5.6.3's closed formula: 0, 0, 1, 5, 10, 9, 18, 35, 38, 76, 81, 91, 120, 169, 195, 227, 272, 272, 347, 368, 436, 490. On 𝕐*(p) = 𝕏*(p)/V, the images of γ₀, γ₁₇₂₈ and rot₁ are all even exactly when p ≡ 1, 3, 13, 15 mod 16, as Theorem 5.6.6 states. Also: the review's q = 13, t = 7 example (one Aut⁺(Π)-orbit of size 112 = 16·7), and the identity (AB − BA)/2 · A · ((AB − BA)/2)⁻¹ = A⁻¹ on 27,897 random pairs (finding 1).

Recomputed or re-derived: E1, E2, E3, E4 (ℤ/3: orbit 8, coarse degree 4), E6 (genus 1 at p = 11), E7 and E31 (−2 is not admissible for p = 2, 3), E25, E26, E27, E32 (τ₁₂ fixes (3,3,3), R₃ does not), E34 (𝕄(F₃) = {0} ∪ {(±1,±1,±1)}, with the eight nonzero points one orbit). findings.claim: The last sentence of Theorem 5.6.4 ('for p ≥ 13, p ∉ E_bgs and any number field K, only finitely many elliptic curves admit a SL₂(F_p)-structure with ramification index 2p') and of Theorem 1.2.9 ('… only finitely many elliptic curves admit a SL₂(F_p)-cover with ramification index 2p') are false read over K, and item 16 states them over K ('only finitely many elliptic curves over K admit an SL₂(F_p)-cover …'), item 97 likewise. The proof applies Faltings' theorem to the coarse curve M̄_p, so it bounds only the K-points of M̄_p, i.e. the j-invariants. Quadratic twists defeat the literal statement. (i) γ_{−I} acts trivially on Epi^ext(Π, SL₂(F_p))_{−2}: for A, B ∈ SL₂(F_p) with t := tr[A,B] ≠ 2 (p odd), M := (AB − BA)/2 has det M = (2 − t)/4, so for t = −2, M ∈ SL₂(F_p), and M A M⁻¹ = A⁻¹, M B M⁻¹ = B⁻¹. So ϕ∘γ_{−I} is Inn(SL₂(F_p))-conjugate to ϕ. (ii) The automorphism [−1] of E fixes O and acts on H₁(E, ℤ) by −1; by Nielsen's theorem its outer class on Π is that of γ_{−I}. For the quadratic twist E^d the outer Galois representation of Theorem 2.5.2(3) changes by [−1]_* on the elements σ with χ_d(σ) = −1, which by (i) act trivially on Epi^ext(·, SL₂(F_p))_{−2}. So T_G(E^d/K) = T_G(E/K) for G = SL₂(F_p) at trace −2. (iii) Such structures exist over suitable K: for any E over a number field with j(E) ∉ {0, 1728}, Galois acts on the finite fibre Epi^ext(Π, SL₂(F_p))_{−2} through a finite quotient, so over a finite extension K every point of the fibre is K-rational. The E^d, d ∈ K^×/K^×², are pairwise non-isomorphic over K since j ∉ {0, 1728}. So for such K infinitely many elliptic curves over K carry an SL₂(F_p)-structure with ramification index 2p. The cover version fails too. A G-equivariant lift ι of [−1] to the torsor X → E° exists by (i), with ι² ∈ Z(G) = {±I}. With g = [[0,1],[−1,0]] (g² = −I), ι or ι∘r_g is an involutive lift of [−1], rational over K after a finite extension, and descending along it gives a K-rational geometrically connected SL₂(F_p)-cover of each E^d, with the same ramification 2p. What the proof establishes is finiteness of j(E) ∈ K, that is, of K̄-isomorphism classes. The author's 2025 survey (arXiv:2510.12003v1, Corollary 5.29, p. 57) repeats the statement in the cover form ('only finitely many elliptic curves over K admit a geometrically connected SL₂(F_p)-cover with ramification index 2p defined over K').
findings.evidence: arXiv v2, Theorem 5.6.4, p. 84: 'In particular, for p ≥ 13, p ∉ E_bgs and any number field K, only finitely many elliptic curves admit a SL₂(F_p)-structure with ramification index 2p. Proof. … The finiteness follows from the first by Falting's theorem.' Theorem 1.2.9, p. 8: 'by Falting's theorem, for any p ≥ 13, p ∉ E_bgs, and any number field K, only finitely many elliptic curves admit a SL₂(F_p)-cover with ramification index 2p.' Theorem 2.5.2(3), p. 25: T_G(E/S) ≅ {ϕ ∈ Epi^ext(π₁(E°_s̄, x̄), G) | ϕ∘ρ_{E,x̄}(σ) = ϕ for all σ}. Theorem 2.5.2(5), p. 26: α : Out(Π) → GL(H₁(E, ℤ)) is an isomorphism (Nielsen). The identity M A M⁻¹ = A⁻¹, M B M⁻¹ = B⁻¹ for M = (AB − BA)/2, with det(AB − BA) = 2 − tr[A,B], was checked on 27,897 random pairs with tr[A,B] ≠ 2 over F_p for p ∈ {5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 29, 31, 101}, with no failure. It is the classical fact that a traceless M ∈ SL₂ satisfies M² = −I and M X M⁻¹ = X⁻¹ for X in the span of A, B with tr(MA) = tr(MB) = 0. Item 16: '… for p ≥ 13, p ∉ E_bgs, and any number field K, only finitely many elliptic curves over K admit an SL₂(F_p)-cover branched only over the origin with ramification index 2p.' Item 97: '… hence for p ≥ 13, p ∉ E_bgs and any number field K only finitely many elliptic curves admit an SL₂(F_p)-structure with ramification index 2p.'

findings.claim: All 38 source issues, and every statement correction, rest on arXiv v2 (19 June 2021). The version of record, Ann. of Math. 199 (2024) 301–443, is a later text. The Annals page records 'Received: 18 June 2021, Revised: 28 July 2022, Accepted: 8 August 2022', a revision more than a year after v2 that nobody has read. Three things follow. (a) PROTOCOL section 18 requires sourceVersions as soon as a finding has affects 'a stated result'. Six do, and the file has none: scripts/check_errata.py reports 'sourceVersions is required when a finding quotes a stated result'. (b) The collation worklist should list the paper, but data/collation.json classifies it as read from the published text ('PAPER-CHEN-24': 'published'), so REQUESTS.md omits it. scripts/collation.py falls back on the free-text 'searched' notes. The regex PUBLISHER matches 'annals.math' and READ_IT matches the words 'published version' in 'the published version is behind the journal's paywall and could not be read'. So a note saying the text was not read counts as having read it. (c) The corrections to stated results (the reversed condition of Theorem 1.1.2, p ≥ 5 in Theorems 1.2.9 and 5.5.7(b), non-injectivity of Tr_*, Lemma 6.1.3, Proposition 6.1.4), and finding 1 above, may already be fixed in print. Their 'known': 'new' is unverified.

findings.claim: The Hurwitz stack of G-Galois covers of n-pointed genus-g curves, branched only at the markings, is now planned in three places. (1) IG.5 plans 'the relevant Hurwitz moduli with braid/Nielsen-class components', and PAPER-LIU-WOOD-ZUREICKBROWN-24/30 routes the Hurwitz stacks Hur^n_G there. (2) PAPER-LANDESMAN-LITT-24/125 routes to its new roadmap 'the Hurwitz stack of H-Galois covers of n-pointed genus g curves unramified outside the marked points. It is a Deligne–Mumford stack, étale over M_{g,n}, whose points have isotropy groups isomorphic to the centre Z(H)' [Wewers]. (3) Chen's route 6 plans, for (g, n) = (1, 1), the same object and the same two properties. Adm⁰(G) → M(1) is étale (Proposition 2.5.3, item 36). Its vertical automorphism groups are Z(G) (Proposition 2.5.6, item 39). Rigidifying by Z(G) gives the finite étale M(G) (Proposition 2.5.10(b), items 34, 35, 41). Items 21, 23 and 33 are stated for arbitrary (g, n): admissible G-covers of prestable n-pointed curves, Adm‾_{g,n}(G), and the equivalence H‾_{g,n,G} ≅ Adm‾^{conn}_{g,n}(G). So the general notion would be built by two new roadmaps whose designs are both pending, and by IG.5, contrary to PROTOCOL section 15: plan a general notion 'once, in the most general form those uses require, in the roadmap that owns it'. My red team of PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 (finding 3) assigned the Hurwitz action and Hurwitz covering spaces to IG.3/IG.5. That concerned different items. This finding rests on the (1,1)/(g,n) overlap shown here, not on that verdict.

findings.claim: The source routes accepted on 23 September 2026 have not reached the blueprint jobs they target, and one already closed without them. Live issue #1025 (BP-ClassicalArithmeticCompletion) lists as maintainer-added sources only Bennett–Siksek and Martin, both accepted on 22 September. #1013 (BP-InverseGalois…) lists only Harpaz–Wittenberg. #1020 (BP-Anabelian…) lists only Balakrishnan–Dogra–Müller–Tuitman–Vonk. None names this paper. The CA blueprint's second pass (24 September, commit e810b287, 'with Bennett–Siksek and Martin covered') marked CA.4 source_decomposed. Its sources are Martin, Bourgain–Gamburd–Sarnak and two Zhang papers, and every Markoff node uses the coefficient-three equation x₀² + x₁² + x₂² = 3x₀x₁x₂. Nothing in the atlas plans the trace-coordinate surface 𝕏 : x² + y² + z² = xyz, the twist ξ : 𝕄 → 𝕏, (x, y, z) ↦ (3x, 3y, 3z), with its isomorphism over ℤ[1/3] and bijection 𝕄(ℤ) ≅ 𝕏(ℤ), or Markoff's theorem in the 𝕏-normalisation (items 9, 10, 90). Yet the route 2 brief tells the Part II to 'Import the Markoff carrier — the surfaces x²+y²+z²−xyz = 0 and x²+y²+z²−3xyz = 0, …, the twist between the two normalisations and Markoff's theorem — from ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.4', and the route 6 brief says the same. Both designs would import something CA.4 does not provide. Separately, the route 6 brief imports from 'ArithmeticDynamicsPartIIMarkoff … whose design job is pending'. That job is superseded, 'folded into DESIGN-ArithmeticDynamicsPartII: one design per Part II parent (2026-09-28)', and the roadmap id is now ArithmeticDynamicsPartII (issue #3367). This rests on the same mechanism as my red team of Gamburd–Magee–Ronan 19 (finding 7, confirmed), which showed CA.4 closed without that paper. The point here is new: this paper's coefficient-one carrier and twist are missing from CA.4 while two briefs import them.

findings.claim: Several inputs the paper cites for load-bearing steps have neither a prerequisite entry nor an item. (a) Brumfiel–Hilden, SL(2) representations of finitely presented groups (Contemp. Math. 187, 1995). It is the only source given for: Theorem 5.2.1 over an arbitrary ring R, where 'A[Π]^{GL₂(R)} = R[A, B, C]' is [BH95, Propositions 3.5 and 9.1(ii)] (item 77); Lemma 5.2.4, the trace of the commutator (item 78); and Lemma 5.2.9, the absolute-irreducibility criterion A² + B² + C² − ABC − 4 ∈ R^× (item 79). The Fricke–Vogt statement is classical only over ℂ. (b) Deligne 1989, Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points, §15. §4.2 'follow[s] Deligne [Del89, §15]' for tangential base points and the analytic comparison (items 56–58, routed to NC.0). The NC packet's three sources do not include it. (c) Magnus–Karrass–Solitar and Osborne–Zieschang, cited for the Nielsen generators and Nielsen's theorem (finding 3). (d) Knudsen 1983, for M_{g,n} and the forgetful maps (item 119). Two small inputs also have no item. (e) Invariance of π₁ under extension of algebraically closed fields [SGA 1, XIII, Proposition 4.6] with GAGA [SGA 1, XII]. Remark 4.2.4 uses them to transport the analytic existence of symmetric good paths, and the §4 analysis, from ℂ to an arbitrary algebraically closed k of characteristic 0 (the standing hypothesis of §4). (f) The group theory in the proof of Corollary 5.6.8: the composition factors of SL₂(ℤ/n) are abelian or PSL₂(F_ℓ) with ℓ ≥ 5, and a finite cover of a noncongruence modular stack is noncongruence.

Remark 4.2.4, p. 46: 'if L/K is an extension of algebraically closed fields … the map X_L → X induces an isomorphism on fundamental groups … [Gro71, Exposé XIII, Proposition 4.6] … classical GAGA results [Gro71, Exposé XII]'. Proof of Corollary 5.6.8, p. 85: 'the composition factors of SL₂(ℤ/n) are either abelian or of the form PSL₂(F_p) for primes p ≥ 5'; 'a cover of a noncongruence modular stack is noncongruence'. findings.claim: Two misprints are not recorded. (a) The introduction says the combinatorial integer satisfies 'm_X divides m′_X, and … m′_X differs from m_X by at most a factor of 12'. What §3.5 proves, and what the proof of Theorem 4.10.5 uses, is the other direction: m′_X | m_X and m_X | 12m′_X. 'm_X | m′_X' together with m′_X | m_X would force equality, contradicting 'differs … by at most a factor of 12'. (b) The proof of Corollary 4.12.4 ends 'Similarly, (c) immediately follows from Lemma 4.12.2 and Vdovin's theorem', but the corollary has only parts (a) and (b). The sentence proves the second bullet of (b).
findings.evidence: arXiv v2, §1.3.2, p. 10: 'This will yield an integer m′_X, defined purely combinatorially, such that m_X divides m′_X, and such that m′_X differs from m_X by at most a factor of 12.' §3.5, p. 42: 'then 12m_X kills all the automorphism groups of geometric points, so we must have m_X | 12m′_X. In fact … the local characters of σ*Ω_{C′/R} restrict to faithful representations of the vertical automorphism groups, so up to a factor of 12, m_X is equal to m′_X' (faithfulness gives m′_X | m_X). Proof of Theorem 4.10.5, p. 62: 'the full automorphism groups are killed by 12m′'. Corollary 4.12.4, p. 64: parts (a) and (b) only; its proof: 'Part (a) follows from Lemma 4.12.2. For (b), … Similarly, (c) immediately follows from Lemma 4.12.2 and Vdovin's theorem.'
